key_insight: Chest X-ray foundation models trained on adult data lose substantial accuracy when applied to pediatric cases, and deeper adaptation does not reliably fix this domain shift.
clinical_relevance: Adult-to-child transfer in medical imaging may require pediatric-specific validation or retraining, because strong adult performance may not generalize to children.
method: Harmonized VinDr-CXR and PediCXR into a five-label chest X-ray classification task
Benchmarked six foundation models plus two CNN baselines
Compared linear probing, partial fine-tuning, and full fine-tuning using adult data only
evidence_signal: Across in-domain and pediatric testing, Macro-AUROC fell from about 92% on adult data to about 78% on pediatric data, with drops exceeding 10 percentage points for all models.
watch_item: The results suggest that high adult test performance should not be assumed to indicate safe or reliable pediatric deployment without dedicated external validation.
paper_title: From Adults to Children: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Chest X-Ray Classification under Domain Shift
